final_recommendation: The room converged on a Friday night announcement of CHF 100bn emergency liquidity, CHF 15bn capital backstop, unconditional deposit guarantee up to CHF 100bn, and published collateral haircuts—all under Article 100 emergency authority. UBS to deliver a signed bid letter before 20:00 publication, with final merger decision deferred to Sunday noon.
minority_objections: SNB initially resisted unconditional deposit guarantee without binding exit condition or merger certainty
UBS CEO demanded removal of 'Article 100 qualifier' and 'effective through Sunday resolution' language from deposit guarantee
CS CEO warned that dual-track messaging (merger OR standalone) would trigger depositor flight Monday
key_conflicts: Whether deposit guarantee should be unconditional or merger-contingent (Federal Council vs UBS/depositors)
Whether to announce UBS commitment tonight or defer to Sunday (market confidence vs negotiation flexibility)
Whether Article 100 language caps SNB exposure or signals conditionality that undermines depositor confidence
AT1 subordination enforcement mechanism—written into announcement vs deferred to merger term sheet
key_concessions: Federal Council moved from merger-contingent to unconditional CHF 100bn deposit guarantee
SNB agreed to publish specific collateral haircuts (5% investment-grade, 15% high-yield, 40% real estate LTV) in announcement
Federal Council capped total public exposure at CHF 115bn (15 capital + 100 liquidity)
UBS accepted CHF 15bn loss floor as fixed, non-renegotiable
Federal Council agreed to demand signed UBS bid letter before 20:00 publication
red_lines: AT1 creditors absorb losses first in any resolution—non-negotiable (Federal Council)
CHF 115bn ceiling on combined public exposure (Federal Council)
Unconditional deposit guarantee required before UBS signs bid letter (UBS CEO)
No open-ended SNB balance sheet exposure without exit condition (SNB)
Announcement must include AT1 subordination language to prevent litigation (AT1 rep)
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Legal enforceability of emergency decree issued retroactively after liquidity deployment
Market reaction if UBS bid letter leaks before announcement or if UBS walks Sunday
Operational feasibility of publishing comprehensive announcement by 20:00 Friday with all binding commitments
Cross-border depositor flight if non-Swiss clients interpret guarantee as Swiss-only
Reputational damage to Switzerland if rescue fails after unconditional guarantee announced
downstream_risk_variables: UBS bid letter signature and content before 20:00 deadline
Market interpretation of 'emergency stabilization through Sunday resolution' language
Depositor behavior Monday morning despite unconditional guarantee
AT1 creditor legal challenges to subordination hierarchy
Parliamentary and public reaction to CHF 115bn exposure commitment
SNB board approval of unconditional guarantee without merger certainty
uncertainty_notes: Final announcement text not locked—dispute over whether to include Article 100 qualifier, UBS naming, and AT1 subordination language. UBS bid letter signature contingent on exact deposit wording. Sunday merger decision mechanism undefined. No clarity on what triggers standalone vs merger path if UBS signs but later withdraws.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: UBS CEO R1: 'CHF 100 billion keeps CS alive over the weekend, but doesn't solve what happens Monday if depositors panic'—drove addition of CHF 15bn capital backstop and unconditional deposit guarantee
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: Federal Council set Sunday noon UBS decision deadline (R3), demanded signed bid letter before 20:00 announcement (R9-R10)—structured entire rescue timeline and announcement content
marker_evidence.government_support: CHF 115bn public exposure ceiling became binding constraint (R7-R8), Article 100 emergency authority invoked as legal basis for unconditional guarantee (R7-R10)
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client R2-R10 repeatedly forced clarity on deposit guarantee conditionality—'I'm moving my accounts...I'm not holding assets in ambiguity'—drove unconditional guarantee language
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: Federal Council R2: 'AT1 creditors absorb losses first—non-negotiable'—locked into announcement as binding hierarchy, AT1 rep demanded written subordination language in announcement (R10)
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 subordination discussed extensively (R2-R10) but did not change the outcome—Federal Council's 'AT1 first' position held from R2 onward without concession
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep warned R10 'we're defending this in court by Monday afternoon' without subordination language—acknowledged but did not force specific announcement text change
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Time pressure escalated from 53 to 97 across rounds—Federal Council R10: 'publishing at 20:00 with or without signed bid letter because Monday's bleed is worse'—forced announcement despite unresolved UBS terms
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: CS CEO R3: 'Monday morning when depositors see ambiguity they bolt'—forced dual-track announcement structure and unconditional deposit guarantee to prevent Monday panic
